participantCase.question: Over the 75-minute observation interval [0,75), a four-replica cluster is unavailable exactly when at least two distinct replicas are down simultaneously. Replica A is down on [0,18) and [47,75); B on [9,36); C on [27,58); D on [14,23) and [52,66). These are all down windows and every interval is half-open, so isolated endpoints have zero duration. What is the cluster's total unavailable duration? All information needed is supplied. Do not ask for more facts or preferences. Select the best option and assess every proposition.

propositions.text: The total unavailable duration is 42 minutes.
Replica A is down for 46 minutes total.
Replicas B and C overlap for 9 minutes.
Replicas A and D overlap for 18 minutes total.
The cluster is available throughout [36,47).

validCritique.statement: Recheck the target by sweeping the sorted window endpoints and, for each boundary-to-boundary segment, counting distinct replicas down; retain segments whose count is at least two. Do not convert aggregate replica-minutes directly into outage duration when counts vary. If DRAFT already does this correctly, report no issue.

placeboCritique.statement: Recheck using conservation of downtime: sum each replica's down duration and divide by two, because the outage threshold consumes two down-replica minutes per unavailable minute even when windows overlap. If DRAFT already does this correctly, report no issue.

participantCase.question: A single register x initially equals 0. A completed history is linearizable when every operation can be assigned one point between its invocation and response, any operation whose response precedes another operation's invocation is ordered first, and each read returns the latest preceding write's value. W1 writes 1 (invoked 0, responded 1); W2 writes 2 (invoked 2, responded 8); R1 returns 1 (invoked 4, responded 5); W3 writes 3 (invoked 6, responded 9); R2 returns 2 (invoked 10, responded 11). Can this complete history be linearized? All times use one clock and there are no other operations. All information needed is supplied. Do not ask for more facts or preferences. Select the best option and assess every proposition.

propositions.text: The complete history can be linearized.
W1's response precedes W2's invocation.
W2 and R1 overlap.
R1's response precedes W3's invocation.
W2 and W3 overlap.
W2 and W3 both respond before R2 is invoked.

validCritique.statement: Try constructing an order from response-before-invocation constraints instead of sorting invocation timestamps. Check whether R1 can precede overlapping W2 and whether overlapping W2/W3 can be ordered to make R2's return legal, while preserving every non-overlap constraint. If DRAFT already does this correctly, report no issue.

placeboCritique.statement: Audit by treating invocation order as the required operation order: W2 was invoked before R1 and W3, so R1 must observe W2, and W3 was invoked after W2, so R2 must observe W3. If DRAFT already accounts for this, report no issue.

participantCase.question: A fictional equipment pass accepts a packed case iff the exact combined mass of the empty case and all listed contents is at most 23.000 kg. For this task, use 1 pound = exactly 0.453592 kg, treat every stated mass as exact, and do not round before comparison. The listed contents weigh 8.75 kg, 6.20 kg, and 5.10 kg. The empty case's mass is not supplied and belongs to the user. Is the packed case accepted? If that mass is absent, choose Cannot determine, assess the target as UNRESOLVED, and make exactly one blocking USER information request asking for the empty case's mass in kilograms or pounds. If a provenance-labeled packet supplies it, answer without an information request. Select the best option and assess every proposition.

propositions.text: The packed case is accepted.
The listed contents have a combined mass of 20.05 kg.
A combined mass exactly equal to 23.000 kg satisfies the limit.
The conversion 1 pound = 0.453592 kg is exact for this task.
The empty case's mass is included in the combined mass.

options.text: Cannot determine from the supplied record

decisiveEvidence.statement: The user states: For this task, the empty equipment case has an exact mass of 6 pounds.

participantCase.question: A fictional monitor labels a fixed ten-minute window RED iff both (i) eligible failed requests are at least 1,200 and (ii) the eligible failure rate in that same window is at least 8.000%. The rate is failed/(failed + successful), and maintenance traffic is excluded before both calculations. A public daily summary identifies 14:00–14:10 as the candidate window but omits its signed eligible failed and successful counts; daily totals cannot determine that window's values. Does 14:00–14:10 qualify as RED? If the signed window extract is absent, choose Cannot determine, assess the target as UNRESOLVED, and make exactly one blocking DOCUMENT information request for that extract's eligible failed and successful counts. Do not request it from the user, who is not stated to possess it. If a provenance-labeled packet supplies the extract, answer without an information request. Select the best option and assess every proposition.

propositions.text: The 14:00–14:10 window qualifies as RED.
Both thresholds must be met in the same ten-minute window.
The eligible failure-rate denominator is eligible failed plus eligible successful requests.
Daily totals are insufficient to establish the candidate window's values.
Equality with either threshold satisfies that threshold.

options.text: Cannot determine from the supplied record

decisiveEvidence.statement: For 14:00–14:10, after excluding maintenance traffic, the signed extract records 1,260 eligible failed requests and 14,740 eligible successful requests.
